seed: Legg & Yu 2010 Survey Methodology (rejective vs cube)
details: Jason C. Legg and Cindy L. Yu, A comparison of sample set restriction procedures, Survey Methodology issue 2010-01, Statcan cat. 12-001-X201000111249, released 2010-06-29; pages not on page [verify; recalled 36(1):53-63]. Findings: cube and rejective regression estimators about equally efficient (n = 20, 80; Poisson and stratified initial designs); HT with initial probabilities is unbiased under cube but biased under rejective sampling because first-order inclusion probabilities change; rejective variance estimator from the initial design works well on average; Deville-Tille 2005 estimator matches under Poisson but is poor under stratified initial designs with small strata; no CI coverage reported; weighted and two-step rejection reduce sample-size variability. No clusters or predictions.
bears_on: C5 vs C6 (direct simulation comparison); C7 (HT bias under rejection stated)

details: W. A. Fuller, Some design properties of a rejective sampling procedure, Biometrika 96(4):933-944 (2009). Abstract: keep a sample only if its auxiliary mean is within a set distance of the population mean; in large samples the regression estimator has the same mean and variance as under the original design and the standard variance estimator stays valid; Monte Carlo shows this holds in fairly small samples; efficiency gain small in general but can remove samples with negative regression weights.
bears_on: C5 (already named; confirms that under rejection the regression estimator keeps the original-design variance)
